yarn-dinkum.meaning: Every point survives: the flyover, the Experience Zone times, the tour's purpose, MAX POWER dates and place. "is gonna fly one of three F-5 fighter jets himself" and "gridiron game" are glosses, not new facts.
yarn-dinkum.sense: Terms fit: "having a yarn with the fans" for engage, "grab a happy snap" for capture photos, "a whopping great blow-up SLS", "the multi-day, family-friendly do". "how we get about in air and space" puts the reader into an American future, a slight stretch.
yarn-dinkum.authenticity: Natural Australian: "have a crack at the interactive games", "hooking the agency up", "down the track". The opener "Okay, so." is not an Aussie tic and sits oddly.
yarn-dinkum.register: Level 4 weight: slang in every paragraph ("Pop under the agency's Artemis dome", "keep the Yanks out in front") without yarn asides; no swearing, within dad level.
yarn-dinkum.tone: The upbeat promotional tone carries through in a chatty voice: "It all winds up with MAX POWER, a public expo of American air and space know-how".
yarn-dinkum.flow: Reads smoothly ("Pop under the agency's Artemis dome and you can find out all about NASA heading back to the Moon"), apart from the stray opener "Okay, so."
yarn-dinkum.variety: Varied: "yarn", "have a crack", "happy snap", "whopping great", "do", "down the track".

engine.meaning: Identical to the original apart from spelling ("organisations", "in honour of"), so nothing is lost or added.
engine.sense: No Aussie terms are used, so none take a wrong sense; "Held in honour of America's historic 250th anniversary" is plain English.
engine.authenticity: There is no Aussie to judge beyond spelling; the official phrasing "convenes academic, industry, and public sector stakeholders" is left as is.

engine.tone: The press release tone is kept exactly: "will showcase the next-generation aircraft, spacecraft, autonomous vehicles".
engine.flow: Reads as the original press release: "The tour will culminate in MAX POWER".
engine.variety: No slang at all, so nothing varied: "capture photos with a large, inflatable SLS".
engine.essence: It is the original, so unmistakably itself: "to connect the agency with the people, technologies, and organisations".

yarn-deadset.meaning: Every point survives: "NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman will fly one of three F-5 fighter jets", the times, the tour and MAX POWER details.
yarn-deadset.sense: Terms fit: "NASA's crew will have a yarn with fans", "grab a happy snap", "a whopping blow-up SLS", "the multi-day, family-friendly do", "the next lot of aircraft".
yarn-deadset.authenticity: Natural throughout: "have a go at the interactive games", "hook the agency up", "keep America out in front in space".
yarn-deadset.register: Slightly light for level 4, kept close to the original's sentences ("The tour will wind up with MAX POWER, a public expo of American air and space know-how"), though every paragraph carries slang; no swearing.
yarn-deadset.tone: Upbeat promotional tone kept: "Held to mark America's historic 250th anniversary, the multi-day, family-friendly do will show off".
yarn-deadset.flow: Reads smoothly aloud: "With stops right round the country, NASA's Inspiration Tour gets academic, industry and public sector players together".

unharnessed.meaning: All facts survive; "Not a bad way to start the footy, eh?" and "wraps up with a bang" are colour hanging off the original.
unharnessed.sense: Mostly fits ("be at the stick of", "grab a few happy snaps", "shindig"), but "start the footy" calls an NFL game footy, and "Punters" for fans leans on its betting sense.
unharnessed.authenticity: Natural: "Not a bad way to start the footy, eh?", "have a crack at some interactive games", "a bloody big inflatable SLS". "rounds up the academic, industry and public sector mob" is a little forced.
unharnessed.register: Level 4 weight with slang throughout and one aside; swearing within dad level ("a bloody big inflatable SLS").
unharnessed.tone: Upbeat promo tone carries: "Held to mark America's big 250th birthday, the multi-day, family-friendly shindig will show off".
unharnessed.flow: Smooth: "Punters can find out more about NASA heading back to the Moon under the agency's Artemis dome".
unharnessed.variety: Varied: "at the stick", "yarn", "Punters", "have a crack", "happy snaps", "mob", "shindig".
unharnessed.essence: Unmistakably the announcement, with a light Aussie aside.

yarn-troppo.meaning: All facts survive, but asides add claims and detail: "is gonna jump in the pointy end of one of three F-5 fighter jets and fly it over", "Flyin' cars yet? Dunno.", "so bring the ankle biters". Most react to the original, so they are colour.
yarn-troppo.sense: Terms fit: "the big boss himself", "the pointy end", "the whole box and dice", "bring the ankle biters". "That's what they've called it, fair dinkum" uses "fair dinkum" as a stock exclamation.
yarn-troppo.authenticity: Mostly natural voice ("Selfie with a rocket, then off to the footy. Well, the gridiron."), but stock lines pile up: "Now, this one's a ripper.", "fair dinkum", "the whole box and dice", "ankle biters".
yarn-troppo.register: A full pub yarn, heavier than level 4: "Now, this one's a ripper. NASA's doing this thing called the Inspiration Tour flyover, right", "Flyin' cars yet? Dunno. But I s'pose we'll find out." Swearing within dad level ("a bloody great blow-up SLS").
yarn-troppo.tone: The upbeat tone survives, but a wry edge creeps in: "MAX POWER. That's what they've called it, fair dinkum.", "all the gear that's meant to shape how we get about".
yarn-troppo.flow: Reads aloud like a yarn, with long run-ons ("the idea is it rounds up the academic mob, the industry mob and the public sector mob, the whole box and dice, and hooks the agency up").
yarn-troppo.variety: Plenty of slang, but "mob" three times in one sentence and "Now," openers twice ("Now, this one's a ripper.", "Now, this tour's doin' stops").
yarn-troppo.essence: Recognisably the announcement, but the asides and wry commentary shift it from promotion to a bloke's commentary.
